name: transmute
declaration: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rules: The argument passed to `transmute::<Src, Dst>` must be valid at type `Src`.
The result of `transmute::<Src, Dst>` must be valid at type `Dst`.
The caller need not ensure alignment of the transmuted values themselves: because `transmute` passes values by value, the compiler ensures that both `Src` and `Dst` are properly aligned.
When transmuting values that point elsewhere, such as pointers, references, or boxes, the caller must ensure proper alignment of the pointed-to values.

In a `const` context, transmuting a pointer to an integer is undefined behavior unless the pointer was originally created from an integer, including through `transmute`, an integer-to-pointer cast, a helper such as `dangling`, or a semantically equivalent conversion such as punning through `repr(C)` union fields. This restriction also applies when the integer is nested inside an array, tuple, struct, or enum; `MaybeUninit<usize>` is not considered an integer type for this restriction.

A pointer constructed by transmuting an integer to a pointer must not be used for non-zero-sized memory accesses; such accesses are currently considered undefined behavior. This also applies when the integer is nested inside an array, tuple, struct, or enum.
Transmuting `*const ()` to `MaybeUninit<usize>` is permitted; `MaybeUninit<usize>` is not considered an integer type for the pointer-to-integer transmutation restrictions.

Calling `assume_init()` on the result of transmuting `*const ()` to `MaybeUninit<usize>` completes the pointer-to-integer transmutation; in a `const` context, this is undefined behavior unless the original pointer was created from an integer.

When using `transmute` to change the inner type of a container's contents, the caller must preserve all of the container's invariants, including any requirements involving element size, alignment, or `TypeId`.
When using `transmute` to change the element type of a `Vec`, the source and destination element types must have equal sizes.
When using `transmute` to change the element type of a `Vec`, the source and destination element types must have equal alignments.
